findings.reason: this arm exists to replace a cycle test an earlier review found unbuildable, and it is still unbuildable, so the node would either ship no mixed-cycle coverage or silently widen `--after` past the mechanism's stated scope.
findings.text: §8's new mixed-cycle arm ("queues request X waiting on `A#s1`, then dispatches request Y for `A#s1` with `--after` X: Y is refused") cannot be built as written, because the mechanism paragraph defines `--after <request-id>` only "for a brief dispatch that has no section", so a request Y that is *for section A#s1* carries no `--after` wait edge, while a section-less brief dispatch is not "for A#s1" and so is never joined to X's wait; either reading leaves no Y->X edge and the asserted cycle cannot arise

findings.reason: without the positive arm the landed-through-`run_ids` path is untested, and the one condition the section was rewritten to get right can be stubbed out while the gate stays green.
findings.text: §8 asserts "Even a `complete` manifest satisfies a wait only once its run has landed" and makes that the crux of the whole section, but every run-wait arm measures only the negative side (a `blocked`/`failed` closure moves to `blocked-upstream`, a `complete`-but-unlanded run stays `awaiting-upstream`); no arm shows a `complete` run that *has* landed moving its waiter to `queued`, so an implementation whose landed predicate never returns true passes the whole done-when

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES`/`MANIFEST_STATUSES`/`parse_manifest` (`reckon/crew/reports.py:126,138,317`), `run_ids` (`reckon/ledger.py:1019`), `_promoted_run_ids` (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:550`, which does call `ledger_module.run_ids`), `parse_plan_ref` (`reckon/_schema.py:276`, regex `[project:]slug[#stage]`, so `B:plan#s2` resolves), `crew dispatch` with `--brief`/`--section` (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1084,1088,1098`) and `TaskNode` (`reckon/crew/node.py:724`) all resolve; the one symbol present nowhere in the tree, `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES`, is the constant §8 itself attributes to §2's implementation (finding already answered).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's newly added mixed-cycle arm cannot be built under §8's own definition of `--after`, and the landed predicate has no positive arm.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8 names `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py`, `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py`, `reckon/crew/node.py` and a new test file, all durable repository paths, and places no evidence in a scratch or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the symbols §8 introduces (`RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES`, the wait derivation, `--after`) are named by mechanism, with no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §8's factual premise checks out: `completed`, `done`, `landed` and `promoted` are all outside `MANIFEST_STATUSES` (`reckon/crew/reports.py:126-140`), so `parse_manifest` refuses them at `reckon/crew/reports.py:735`, and the repair to `complete`-plus-landed is the right one; the mechanism defect is reported under done_when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 carries one deliverable, a queue that respects the roadmap's DAG across plans and projects; the delivered-status repair is part of making a run wait resolvable, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §8's declared edge `s8 -> s2` is the one it needs (`awaiting-upstream`/`blocked-upstream` come from §2), and its consumers `s9` and `s15` both declare `s8`.
